column1: # One row per exercise id EVER minted (live or retired), TAB-separated,
# sorted by id. '#' comments and blank lines are ignored. Read by
# the same structural reader exe:app links, so the registry is always
# checked against exactly what a learner's browser sees.
#   2. promptCount    length (exPrompts ex) for a live row -- the number of
#                      tombstone row: a retired id mints no prompts.
#   3. status         "live"      -- the id names an exercise that exists in
#                      "tombstone" -- the id is retired; it MUST NOT exist in
#   4. first-shipped  the milestone tag (m2, m3, ...) this id (or, for a
#                      tombstone, the row itself) first appeared under.
#   5. note           free text. For a live row, the deck it belongs to.
#                      For a tombstone, WHY it was retired and what replaces
#                      it (an id, or "none" if nothing replaces it).
# never-renumber rule, line 7 of that file):
#   An exercise id is NEVER deleted from this registry, and an id is NEVER
#   reused for a different exercise later. When an exercise is retired, its
#   row is NOT removed -- it is flipped in place from "live" to "tombstone",
#   its promptCount is set to 0, and its note is updated to say why it was
#   retired and which id (if any) replaces it. This is what lets M3's
#   localStorage progress layer, on loading a saved record whose PromptId's
#   exercise-id resolves to a tombstone row, report "this exercise was
#   retired, see <replacement>" instead of treating the record as silently
#   corrupt: "retired" and "corrupt" are different failure modes for a
#   learner and must stay distinguishable forever, which requires every
#   retired id to still be LOOKUP-ABLE here, permanently.
